record.context_brief: Odd-step core partitions with distinct parts
record.original_question: For odd s, is the number of (s, s+2)-core partitions with distinct parts equal to 2^{s−1} as claimed in Conjecture 11.10?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.10. For s odd, the number of (s, s + 2)-core partitions with distinct parts is 2^{s−1}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A partition of a nonnegative integer $n$ is a weakly decreasing sequence $\lambda = (\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \dots, \lambda_k)$ of positive integers with $\lambda_1 + \dots + \lambda_k = n$. The Young diagram of $\lambda$ has, for each cell in row $i$ and column $j$ (with $1 \le j \le \lambda_i$), a hook length equal to the number of cells directly to the right of it in the same row plus the number of cells directly below it in the same column, plus one. For a positive integer $t$, $\lambda$ is called a $t$-core if no hook length of $\lambda$ equals $t$. Given positive integers $s_1, s_2$, $\lambda$ is an $(s_1, s_2)$-core partition if it is simultaneously an $s_1$-core and an $s_2$-core. A partition has distinct parts if $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \dots > \lambda_k$.

Prove or disprove: for every odd positive integer $s$, the number of $(s, s+2)$-core partitions with distinct parts equals $2^{s-1}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (attributed to Amdeberhan/Straub) that the number of $(s,s+2)$-core partitions with distinct parts is $2^{s-1}$ for odd $s$ has been proven. Proofs were given by Yan–Qin–Jin–Zhou, by Zaleski–Zeilberger, and a bijective proof was given by Nath and Sellers, with related work by Straub and Xiong.
